title: Larkspur engagement sketchbook — outbound + objections
content:
Context and quick summary:
- Target: Larkspur Financial (mid-market payments + treasury; US-focused with 2 engineering hubs).
- Why interesting: embedded payments + treasury roadmap; currently building rules engine for risk that could benefit from low-latency, private LLM inference for dispute classification and contract summarization. Potential quick win: nearline dispute triage to reduce manual review by 20-30%.
- Hypothesis: They care about predictable cost and private deployment (SOC2 + KMS). Likely fit for Redwood Dedicated or Private.

Account map (initial, needs validation):
- Head of Product: Mara Ellison — primary champion for fraud/operations integration. (LinkedIn noted ML & payments background)
- VP Eng (Platform): Tom Brenner — cares about infra and data residency; will ask about networking and KMS.
- Head of Risk Ops: Suresh Iyer — buyer for process improvement, will ask about accuracy and auditability.
- Procurement/Legal: Maria Lopez — standard EULA/SLA negotiation.

Signals and open-source intel:
- Job posting (Nov 2024) for "Inference engineer" implies moving models to production.
- Product blog (June 2025) about automating chargeback ops; references model-based scoring but no infra details.
- Security attestation requests in past deals indicate sensitivity to third-party hosted APIs.

Initial outreach plan (3-touch, conservative cadence) — sketch: 
1) Short email (cold) — 5 lines, focus on ops ROI + security option. Call-to-action: 15-minute intro.
2) Follow-up (phone/LinkedIn) — add a one-sentence example of cost/latency improvement we saw with another mid-market payments customer.
3) Value note with pilot proposal + compliance summary PDF.

Draft cold email (keep it personal / low friction):
Subject: small pilot to cut chargeback review time by ~25%
Hi Mara —
Quick note: saw Larkspur's chargeback automation post and thought it might map to a low-effort pilot. We helped another payments company reduce manual dispute triage by ~25% with a one-month pilot (private deploy + KMS).
If you’re open, I can send a 2-slide pilot plan (no NDA) that maps to your ops flow. 15 mins next week?
— Ava

Phone intro script cheatsheet (30–60s):
- Intro + context (1 line).
- Problem we solve (reduce ops load, predictable inference cost, private deployment).
- Quick proof point + ask for 15-min demo to show pilot plan.

Discovery questions (to validate fit):
- How many dispute reviews per month? (volume + avg tokens per record)
- What’s current SLA for triage? Where does latency matter?
- Are you comfortable with hosted vendors, or do you need VPC/on‑prem?
- Any current model/tooling in the loop? (open-source models vs vendor)
- Who would need to sign off on a 3–4 week pilot?

Objections and suggested responses (raw):
- "We already use Vendor X": ask what the pain is (cost/latency/quality) and whether they’ve benchmarked across model variants; offer non-disruptive A/B pilot routing to compare.
- "Security concerns / No external APIs": emphasize Redwood Private/VPC + KMS + audit logs; offer architecture diagram and SOC2 summary; suggest on-prem eval if needed.
- "Too expensive / unclear ROI": show per-ticket unit economics (estimate below) and propose a small scoped pilot focusing on high-volume, high-cost bucket.
- "Integration effort": point to SDK + simple adapter, and offer implementation support from solutions engineering for the pilot.

Rough cost/benefit sketch (numbers are placeholders, update after discovery):
- Current: 12k disputes/month, avg 400 tokens processed per dispute (prompt+context+response).
- Redwood hosted cost (example): $0.0008 per token = $3.84 per dispute => $46k/month. (But we expect caching + batch + quantization can cut unit cost 40% for this workload.)
- Benefit: reduce manual review by 25% = 3k fewer manual tickets. If avg manual cost is $15/ticket => $45k/month saved. Net positive in pilot if accuracy/acceptance meets threshold.

Pilot proposal (one-paragraph outline to put in follow-up):
- 3–4 week technical pilot: ingest a slice of dispute traffic (sanitized) behind VPC; run model variant A vs baseline on a small routing fraction; metrics: precision for "escalate vs auto-resolve", latency p95, cost per 1k decisions; weekly sync + final results. Minimal code changes: adapter + webhook. SE support included.

Open items / TODOs:
- Confirm contact emails for Mara, Tom, Suresh (Priya to validate).
- Replace placeholder cost numbers with current Redwood hosted + dedicated pricing (ask pricing ops).
- Pull current token estimator helper for dispute payloads (engineering).
- Draft 2-slide pilot summary and compliance one-pager (deadline: 11/12).
- Prepare a short architecture drawing for Private deployment (networking + KMS).

Notes to self (informal):
- Avoid heavy product jargon on first contact; keep focus on ops time & compliance.
- If they ask for model names: offer Redwood-verified open models and also bring up quantized variants for cost demo.
- A/B route: easy win if we can show identical/higher accuracy at lower cost.

Potential win criteria (for moving from pilot to contract):
- >=20% reduction in manual reviews with <=5% drop in accuracy on critical classes.
- Predictable unit economics at scale (showing cost per decision at 1M decisions/month).
- Legal OK on data residency and KMS control.

Last quick draft for follow-up message (after no response to cold):
Hi Mara —
Following up on a quick pilot thought (1 month, private deploy). Attached 2 slides that map directly to chargeback triage — one shows estimated ops upside, the other shows security & integration footprint. Could we grab 15 minutes this week?
Thanks,
Ava

End of sketchbook notes. Keep this as living doc — update after first convo.
